hypothesis.03b17729901d66bfb185c753.distinction: Three plausible constructions are shared negation, narrow negation with an affirmative second alternative, and two independently negative alternatives. This first construction requires both absences. The prior shared-negation and conjunctive-negation formulas are logically equivalent, so they do not supply distinct substantive readings. Shared negation is contextually preferable because the preceding sentence identifies profit-making purpose as a business indicator, but the irregular coordination does not settle the interpretation. No additional defensible Boolean reading absent from the prior hypotheses was identified.

citations.quote: What amounts to “carrying on a business in Hong Kong” is not defined in the Ordinance and will need to be determined by reference to the facts of each case, including whether the person is performing an occupation or a duty which requires attention; the activity involves continuity; the activity is capable of making profit; and the activity was carried out for the purpose of making profit.  A genuine single family office arrangement, established to serve the investment needs of members of a single family, which is not being run as a business (i.e. not receiving any income, other than reimbursement of operating expenses from the family) or have the pursuit of profit as its business objective, should not in the ordinary course be considered as carrying on a business from a licensing perspective.  It is also not the SFC’s intent to extend its regulatory oversight to this type of single family office setup.

concerns.question: The supplied income_beyond_reimbursement fact operationalizes the parenthetical but cannot independently represent the broader case-specific assessment of being run as a business, including continuity, occupation or duty, and capability of making profit.
The irregular coordination “which is not … or have” leaves negation attachment uncertain. Separate predicates express the rival outcomes but do not resolve the wording.

The previous disjunction of two absences would require an additional assumption supplying a separate negative to the second alternative. It does not follow from the stated business-only negation and is not retained as that parse.
The Boolean result expresses only antecedent satisfaction. It does not encode “should not in the ordinary course”, regulatory intent, or a complete licensing conclusion.
Does “not” govern both predicates coordinated by “or”, or only “being run as a business”?
Does the anomalous wording “or have” reflect shared negation or an independently affirmative profit-objective alternative?

The supplied facts cannot distinguish the broader, case-specific meaning of being run as a business from the parenthetical income test. Both formulas rely on the expressly retained operational abstraction.
The supplied Boolean facts can express the rival negation attachments, but cannot determine which grammatical interpretation is intended.

The supplied facts do not encode occupation, continuity, capability of profit, or the qualified force of “should not in the ordinary course”. Those considerations remain outside the antecedent predicate and cannot be inferred from its truth value.

The surrounding regulated-activity, carve-out and territorial conditions cannot be evaluated using these three facts. Neither formula determines a licensing trigger, exemption, compliance status or entitlement.
The regulatory-intent sentence does not supply a separate Boolean condition or remove the qualified wording of the preceding conclusion.
Does the preceding “not” govern both coordinated business indicators, or does “or” join independently sufficient negative descriptions?
Does “in the ordinary course” qualify only the licensing-perspective conclusion rather than the disputed antecedent?

The supplied income fact cannot distinguish the parenthetical income test from the broader case-specific assessment of being run as a business. Occupation or duty, continuity, and capability of profit are not represented. A reading treating the parenthetical as illustrative rather than exhaustive would therefore require null formalization under this vocabulary; it cannot be implemented by silently redefining the supplied fact.

The Boolean fragment does not express the qualified force of should not in the ordinary course or regulatory intent. These remain qualifications on the conclusion, not additional encoded antecedent conditions.
The genuine-family fact combines genuineness, single-family status, and investment-serving purpose. It cannot separately test those descriptions or determine family membership.

The three supplied facts cannot determine regulated activity, the intra-group carve-out, territorial scope, or a licensing obligation. Truth and falsity of these antecedent predicates establish neither exemption nor obligation.

The prior four expressions represent three Boolean conditions: negating a disjunction and conjoining the two negations are equivalent. Their separate presentation supplies no additional legal diversity.

No defensible additional attachment was identified that lets the profit-objective branch escape the genuine-single-family-office requirement. The regulatory-intent sentence likewise supplies no express alternative antecedent. These possibilities should not be added merely to increase diversity.
Does the negation govern both coordinated predicates, only the business predicate, or an understood negative in each alternative?
Is the parenthetical intended as an exhaustive operational test of being run as a business, despite the surrounding case-specific factors?
